# Environment contract

Single source of truth for every environment variable Teaching Journey reads:
[`infra/env.contract.ts`](../infra/env.contract.ts). This page, every `.env.example` and
`.gitleaks.toml` are generated from it (`bun run env:generate`; `bun run env:generate --check`
runs in CI and fails on drift). `bun run doctor` validates the local `.env` files against it and
`bun run env:check` compares the variable **names** present on Railway and Vercel with it —
values are never read into logs or docs.

Legend — **Services**: who reads it (`compose` = docker compose + root scripts). **Scope**:
`secret` values are never printed or committed and have a gitleaks rule. **Local**: the value in
`.env.example` (`—` = optional, documented commented-out). **Railway** / **Vercel**: which provider
environments carry it (`prod`, `pr` / `preview`, `both`, `n/a`). **Set by**: see "Where each value
is set".

## Matrix

| Variable | Services | Scope | Local (`.env.example`) | Railway | Vercel | Set by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TJ_PG_PORT` | compose | config | `5432` | n/a | n/a | template | Host port docker compose publishes Postgres on. The single knob for a port conflict: the root scripts derive DATABASE_URL / TEST_DATABASE_URL from it when those are unset. Shell wins over the file (`TJ_PG_PORT=5433 bun run db:up`). |
| `DATABASE_URL` | api, worker, ci, compose | secret | `postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/teaching_journey` | both | n/a | reference | Postgres connection of the app database (pg-boss installs its own `pgboss` schema in it). Locally the compose database; keep the port in sync with TJ_PG_PORT. On Railway a reference to the `postgres` service over the private network. Contains the password: treat as a secret. |
| `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | api, worker, web, ci, compose | secret | `postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/teaching_journey_test` | n/a | n/a | template | Database the test suites and Playwright use (`@tj/db/testing`, docs/testing.md). Tests TRUNCATE tables here, so it must never equal DATABASE_URL. Never read by a running server. |
| `NODE_ENV` | api, worker | config | `development` | both | n/a | template | development \| test \| production. `development` switches on pino-pretty; `production` refuses ENABLE_TEST_ROUTES and ignores the x-tj-workspace-id shim. |
| `PORT` | api, worker | config | `3001` | both | n/a | template | TCP port of Bun.serve: api 3001 (HTTP + SSE), worker 3002 (`/health` only). Railway routes the public domain to the api's PORT; the worker has no public domain. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | api, worker | config | `info` | both | n/a | template | pino level: fatal \| error \| warn \| info \| debug \| trace \| silent. |
| `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | worker | config | `4` | both | n/a | template | Jobs processed concurrently per queue in one worker process (1-64). |
| `WEB_ORIGIN` | api | config | `http://localhost:5173` | both | n/a | manual | Comma-separated exact browser origins allowed by CORS (credentials on) and trusted by better-auth. Locally the Vite dev server; on Railway the Vercel production origin (`https://teaching-journey-web.vercel.app`, later `https://app.<domain>`). |
| `WEB_ORIGIN_PATTERNS` | api | config | — | both | n/a | template | Optional comma-separated origin GLOBS for per-deployment Vercel preview URLs (`*` = one DNS label, no path), e.g. `https://teaching-journey-web-*-omerbresinskis-projects.vercel.app`. Set on Railway production so PR environments (copies of production) inherit it; the api ignores it when no preview origin matches. Unset locally. |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | api | secret | generated by `setup` | both | n/a | generated | Signs session cookies and magic-link tokens; REQUIRED, at least 32 characters. `bun run setup` generates it into apps/api/.env (crypto.randomBytes(32), base64url) and never prints it; `infra/railway/provision.sh` does the same on Railway (`openssl rand -base64 32 \| railway variable set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET --stdin`). Rotating it signs everyone out. |

Once `app.<d>`/`api.<d>` exist, switch production to `lax` + COOKIE_DOMAIN (ADR 0008). |

Never in a local .env. |
| `VITE_API_URL_FALLBACK` | web | config | — | n/a | preview | manual | Vercel Preview only. API origin for preview builds without a PR number (branch pushes) or without a template — point it at the Railway production api (`https://api-production-903f.up.railway.app`). Never in a local .env. |
| `E2E_VERBOSE` | web | config | — | n/a | n/a | manual | Any value makes `playwright.config.ts` pipe api/worker logs at level info instead of discarding them. Shell only. |

| `TURBO_TOKEN` | ci | secret | — | n/a | n/a | manual | Repository secret: Vercel token for the Turborepo remote cache (ADR 0002). Empty = no remote cache. |
| `TURBO_TEAM` | ci | config | — | n/a | n/a | manual | Repository variable: Vercel team slug for the remote cache (`omerbresinskis-projects`). |

## Local-only path

The local stack is **self-contained**: a fresh clone needs Bun, Docker and nothing from Railway,
Vercel or any dashboard. Every value in every `.env.example` targets the compose Postgres and the
only secret (`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`) is generated on your machine. Proven from a clean clone
(TEACH-26):

```sh
git clone <repo> tj && cd tj
find . -name '.env' -o -name '.env.local' | xargs rm -f     # (a clone has none; shown for parity)
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run setup --ci        # .env files from the examples, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET generated, Postgres up, migrated
bun run doctor            # every check PASS (WARN only for optional tooling such as gitleaks)
bun run dev               # api :3001, worker :3002, web :5173

# sign in with the console magic link (MAIL_PROVIDER=console prints the link in the api log):
curl -s -X POST localhost:3001/auth/sign-in/magic-link -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'origin: http://localhost:5173' \
  -d '{"email":"teacher@example.test","callbackURL":"http://localhost:5173/"}'
# open the printed http://localhost:3001/auth/magic-link/verify?token=... URL with a cookie jar:
curl -s -c jar '<printed url>' -o /dev/null            # 302 + Set-Cookie tj.session_token
curl -s -b jar localhost:3001/me                        # 200 {"user":{...},"workspaceId":"..."}
curl -s -b jar -X POST localhost:3001/jobs/ping -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'origin: http://localhost:5173' -d '{"message":"hello","steps":3}'   # {"jobId":"..."}
curl -N -b jar localhost:3001/jobs/<jobId>/events       # queued -> started -> progress -> completed
```

`bun run setup` never overwrites an existing `.env`; `bun run doctor` validates each one against
this contract (missing keys, malformed URLs/ports/enums — values are never printed).

## Where each value is set

- **generated** — random, created for you — locally by `bun run setup` (appended to `apps/api/.env`, never printed), on Railway by `infra/railway/provision.sh` (`openssl rand -base64 32 | railway variable set NAME --stdin`)
  `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`
- **reference** — a Railway reference / template such as `${{postgres.POSTGRES_PASSWORD}}` or `https://${{RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN}}`, seeded by `provision.sh` (`bun scripts/railway-vars.ts <service>` prints the exact list)
  `DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`
- **template** — a plain, non-secret value with a known default — seeded by `provision.sh` / `vercel env add` / `.env.example`
  `TJ_PG_PORT`, `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`, `WEB_ORIGIN_PATTERNS`, `COOKIE_SAMESITE`, `MAIL_PROVIDER`, `EVENTS_MAX_STREAMS_PER_WORKSPACE`, `EVENTS_REPLAY_LIMIT`, `EVENTS_HEARTBEAT_MS`, `EVENTS_POLL_MS`, `VITE_APP_ENV`, `VITE_DEV_API_TARGET`, `CI`, `REQUIRE_TEST_DB`
- **manual** — a human pastes it: OAuth credentials, tokens, real domains. `bun run env:check --fix` prints the exact `railway variable set` / `vercel env add` command (with a placeholder, never a value)
  `WEB_ORIGIN`, `COOKIE_DOMAIN`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ENABLE_TEST_ROUTES`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, `STORAGE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `STORAGE_ROOT`, `STORAGE_PUBLIC_PREFIXES`, `VITE_API_URL`, `RAILWAY_PR_API_URL_TEMPLATE`, `VITE_API_URL_FALLBACK`, `E2E_VERBOSE`, `CI_STRICT`, `TURBO_TOKEN`, `TURBO_TEAM`

Expected names per provider target (what `bun run env:check` verifies):

- Railway `api` / `production`: `DATABASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `WEB_ORIGIN`, `WEB_ORIGIN_PATTERNS`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `COOKIE_DOMAIN`, `COOKIE_SAMESITE`, `MAIL_PROVIDER`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`
- Railway `api` / `ai-teacher-pr-<n>`: `DATABASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `WEB_ORIGIN`, `WEB_ORIGIN_PATTERNS`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `COOKIE_SAMESITE`, `MAIL_PROVIDER`
- Railway `worker` / `production`: `DATABASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`
- Railway `worker` / `ai-teacher-pr-<n>`: `DATABASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`
- Vercel `teaching-journey-web` / `production`: `VITE_API_URL`, `VITE_APP_ENV`
- Vercel `teaching-journey-web` / `preview`: `VITE_APP_ENV`, `RAILWAY_PR_API_URL_TEMPLATE`, `VITE_API_URL_FALLBACK`

Railway post-provisioning checklist (values, never in git; `infra/railway/provision.sh` seeds the
`reference`/`template` ones from this contract via `scripts/railway-vars.ts`):

```sh
bun scripts/railway-vars.ts api        # NAME=value lines provision.sh passes to `railway variable set`
bun scripts/railway-vars.ts worker
bun run env:check                      # names on production vs this matrix; --fix prints the commands
bun run env:check --pr <n> --fix       # same for an open PR environment
```

## Rotating a secret

Secret-scoped variables: `DATABASE_URL`, `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`, `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, `TURBO_TOKEN`.

1. Generate the new value **without printing it**, e.g. `openssl rand -base64 32 > /tmp/secret` (or let the provider's console generate it).
2. Set it in the provider, values via stdin so nothing lands in shell history or logs:
   - Railway: `railway variable set NAME --stdin --service api < /tmp/secret` (repeat with `--environment ai-teacher-pr-<n>` for an open PR environment; `--skip-deploys` to batch, then `railway redeploy --service api --yes`).
   - Vercel: `vercel env rm NAME production --yes && vercel env add NAME production --sensitive < /tmp/secret` — then redeploy.
   - GitHub Actions: `gh secret set NAME --repo OmerBresinski/ai-teacher < /tmp/secret`.
3. `rm /tmp/secret`; run `bun run env:check` — it compares **names only** and confirms nothing is missing or extra.
4. Locally: delete the line from the relevant `.env` and run `bun run setup` (regenerates `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`) or paste the new value; `bun run doctor` names any missing key.
5. `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` rotation invalidates every session cookie and pending magic link — announce it. `DATABASE_URL` rotation means changing `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` on the `postgres` service; the api/worker reference picks the new value up on redeploy.

`.gitleaks.toml` (generated from the same contract) makes the pre-commit hook and the CI `secrets` job fail on `NAME=<long value>` for every secret-scoped name; `.env`, `.env.*` (except `.env.example`) are gitignored at every level.

## PR environments

A pull request gets a Vercel preview (`apps/web`) and, once Railway billing is active, a Railway
PR environment `ai-teacher-pr-<n>` that copies `production`'s services and variables and gives the api its own
Postgres and domain (`infra/README.md` → "PR environments").

- Reference variables (`DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`) resolve inside the PR environment, so nothing is copied by hand.
- The PR api must accept the preview origin and set a cross-site cookie: `WEB_ORIGIN_PATTERNS` (glob of the Vercel preview URLs) and `COOKIE_SAMESITE=none` are the two PR-only values in the matrix (`railway = pr` / `both`).
- The Vercel preview points at the PR api through `RAILWAY_PR_API_URL_TEMPLATE` (`{pr}` → PR number) resolved by `scripts/vercel-env.ts`; `VITE_API_URL_FALLBACK` covers branch builds without a PR.
- `bun run env:check --pr <n>` compares the names on `ai-teacher-pr-<n>` against the matrix (`railway variable list --environment ai-teacher-pr-<n>`).
